what_its_for: Polyethylene Glycol 400 (PEG 400) is used to relieve occasional constipation. It works by drawing water into your stool to make it softer and easier to pass. It is also used as a base in some eye drops, skin creams, and ointments to help deliver medicine to the area that needs it.
how_to_take: If you are using PEG 400 as a laxative powder: Measure the correct dose using the cap or measuring spoon provided. Stir the powder completely into 4 to 8 ounces (about half a cup to one full cup) of water, juice, coffee, or any other beverage until fully dissolved before drinking. Do not take it as a dry powder. If you are using it in an eye drop or topical product, follow the specific directions on that product's label.
dosing: For constipation in adults and children 17 years and older: The usual dose is 17 grams (about 1 heaping tablespoon) once a day. Do not use more than directed. Do not use for longer than 7 days without talking to your doctor first. For children under 17, always ask your doctor before using. Always follow your doctor's instructions or the directions on the package label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the container tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in a bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this medicine for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid taking it with other laxatives unless your doctor approves. Do not use if you have been told you have a bowel blockage (intestinal obstruction). Avoid giving this product to children under 17 without a doctor's guidance. If you are on a restricted sodium or sugar diet, check with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: severe stomach pain or cramping, bloating that does not go away, nausea or vomiting, bloody or black stools, a sudden change in your bowel habits that lasts more than 2 weeks, or if you have not had a bowel movement after using this medicine for 3 days. Also contact your doctor if you notice any signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: Most people have a bowel movement within 1 to 3 days after starting polyethylene glycol. It does not work right away like some other laxatives. Be patient and continue taking it daily as directed. If you do not see results within 3 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Children under 17: Do not use without a doctor's recommendation and supervision. Older adults: Generally safe to use, but check with your doctor if you have kidney problems, heart problems, or are on a fluid-restricted diet. People with kidney or heart disease: Talk to your doctor first, as changes in fluid and electrolyte balance may be a concern with prolonged use.
